paper_metadata.title: Prognosis of Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy with eye-closure sensitivity

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the recruitment setting (tertiary center) and inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, it uses a convenience sample from a specialized clinic, which may not represent the general JME population, and the participation rate of eligible vs. non-eligible patients is not explicitly detailed.

items.reasoning: The source population is clearly identified as patients from a specific tertiary epilepsy center.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (ECS) was measured using a highly rigorous Video-EEG Neuropsychological Protocol (VNPP) which is superior to standard EEG. The criteria for ECS and EM were clearly defined and applied uniformly.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Eye closure sensitivity (ECS) is a unique EEG phenomenon described as the non-incidental appearance of transient epileptic abnormalities following the closure of the eyes for 1–4s during a standard EEG recording
items.reasoning: The study provides a precise definition of ECS and the clinical expression (EM).

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Group 1 included 22 JME patients with ECS and EM confirmed by VNPP... all patients had a 4–6 h video-EEG monitoring
items.reasoning: The use of a 4-6 hour video-EEG protocol with specific activation tasks is a gold-standard approach for this condition.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: We considered activation as the increase by twice of the number of seizures or epileptic discharges (ED), in comparison to the baseline
items.reasoning: The study uses a pre-defined, standard threshold for 'activation'.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: all patients had a 4–6 h video-EEG monitoring, comprehending a research protocol approved by our Ethics Committee.
items.reasoning: The VNPP was applied consistently to all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes were measured using seizure diaries, which are standard but prone to recall bias. While the clinical follow-up was long, the study does not mention if the clinicians assessing the outcomes were blinded to the ECS status (Group 1 vs Group 2).

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The frequency of seizures was monitored by standard seizure calendars... Freedom of all seizures [was assessed].
items.reasoning: Seizure frequency and seizure freedom are clearly defined as the primary outcomes.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The frequency of seizures was monitored by standard seizure calendars.
items.reasoning: Seizure calendars are standard but subjective. There is no mention of blinding the outcome assessors to the prognostic factor.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement

items.evidence_snippet: All patients were followed-up... The frequency of seizures was monitored by standard seizure calendars.
items.reasoning: The same monitoring method (calendars) was used for both groups.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study measured several important confounders (age of onset, family history, psychiatric comorbidities) and used AED load to account for treatment intensity. However, it did not perform multivariable adjustment (e.g., Cox regression) to control for these factors simultaneously when assessing the independent effect of ECS on prognosis.
